survivors.crates/genui-core/src/patch.rs:361:33: r: Equivalent: this counter is the insert prefix of the current (parent, slot) edit group. It is only read as the estimated retained detach position for later siblings. Detach rejects the hint unless the child at that index is the node being moved, so a smaller estimate is either exactly the true index or rejected without applying an op. Multiplying instead of incrementing can only keep the estimate at or below the true index (never above it), so it cannot silently detach a different node; later estimates stay at or below their true positions for the same reason. The final tree and the emitted ops are unchanged.

Equivalent: the guarded body calls visit_effects(Some(&stop), previous_stop). ResourceIndex::visit only descends where key > after and key <= until, so it visits the interval (stop, previous]. When stop == previous that interval is empty, so the == mutant (which fires only on equality) performs no visits; when stop < previous the original fires and the mutant does not, but only the original is reachable for a non-empty interval.

Equivalent: the guarded call visits (stop, previous], which is empty when stop > previous. The > mutant therefore fires only on an inverted interval and performs no visits; the original branch already covers every non-empty deactivation interval.

Equivalent: <= adds only the stop == previous case to the original condition. The visited interval (stop, previous] is empty for equal endpoints, so the extra call visits nothing and emits no deactivation.
Equivalent: the guarded body calls visit_materialized(Some(&previous), stop), whose range is (previous, stop]. It is empty when stop == previous, so firing only on equality visits nothing.

Equivalent: an inverted interval (previous > stop) visits nothing in visit_materialized/visit_effects, so the < mutant fires only when there is nothing to activate and never replaces a real activation.
Equivalent: >= differs from > only when stop == previous, where the materialized interval (previous, stop] is empty. The extra traversal activates and counts nothing.

Equivalent: this filter only runs over keys of old.graph.locations.changed_keys(&new.graph.locations). Any such id that exists in only one node map is already in `ids`, because before.nodes.changed_keys(&after.nodes) reports that Add/Remove key unconditionally.
